title: Holden: pure spirit by natural reason knows all corporeal natures and motions—denying prayer-hearing is crass ignorance
source_text: XLIII. Imo Henricus Holden Doctor Parisiensis affirmat ipsa ratione naturali demonstrari posse, quod quivis pure Spiritus perfecte cognoscat & intelligat, rerum omnium corporearum naturas, motus & actiones omnes: ac propterea ignorantiam crassam bardamque tribuit illis, qui existimant Sanctos in caelo regnantes non audire mortalium preces. In Divinae fidei analysi lib. 2. cap. 7.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed Henry Holden, Doctor of Paris, affirms that it can be demonstrated by natural reason itself that any purely spiritual being perfectly knows and understands the natures, motions, and all actions of all corporeal things: and therefore he attributes a crass and dull ignorance to those who think that the Saints reigning in heaven do not hear the prayers of mortals. In the Analysis of Divine Faith, book 2, chapter 7.
pass_b_english: Holden (Paris): natural reason shows a pure spirit knows every corporeal nature, motion, and act.
Calling heaven deaf to mortal prayer is, for him, dense ignorance.

choices.why: Named Paris doctor for natural-reason claim about spirit cognition.
